blogs.title: The Early Bird Gets the Stroke: Unmasking Preoperative Heparin Exposure as the Trigger for Post-CABG HIT
blogs.description: This post explores the critical diagnostic pitfall of 'early-onset' HIT (platelet drop < POD 5) in cardiac surgery patients. We will analyze how a seemingly innocuous preoperative catheterization procedure involving unfractionated heparin can prime the immune system, leading to rapid thrombocytopenia immediately upon re-exposure during bypass. The discussion focuses on refining the 4Ts score interpretation in the perioperative setting and emphasizes the necessity of a meticulous medication history extending beyond just the hospital admission.

blogs.title: Beyond Classic Serotonin Release: Decoding Atypical SRA Profiles in Autoimmune HIT
blogs.description: Focusing on the laboratory diagnostics, this article dissects the complex Serotonin Release Assay (SRA) results seen in autoimmune HIT (aHIT). We will interpret why strong platelet activation occurs at zero heparin concentration and discuss the significance of 'partial resistance' to Fc receptor blocking antibodies. Clinicians will learn how to recognize these 'indeterminate' patterns that often lead to false negatives or delayed diagnoses, distinguishing them from classic heparin-dependent HIT.
blogs.,title: When Argatroban Isn't Enough: Managing Severe Hypercoagulability and Consumptive Coagulopathy in aHIT
blogs.description: This case illustrates a severe variant of HIT where standard anticoagulation fails to halt a destructive cycle of microvascular thrombosis. We will examine the clinical signs of consumptive coagulopathy (falling fibrinogen, rising D-dimers, schistocytosis) occurring despite therapeutic argatroban levels. The post covers the strategic rationale for switching to fondaparinux, including the use of antithrombin supplementation, and discusses why high-dose IVIG may yield a blunted response in these hyper-reactive cases.

blogs.title: The Spectrum of Recovery: Temporal Evolution of Antibody Phenotypes from Autoimmune to Classic HIT
blogs.description: Autoimmune HIT is not static; this post follows the longitudinal serological evolution of our patient over four months. We will track how the dominant antibody population shifted from heparin-independent activation (characteristic of aHIT) back to a classic heparin-dependent profile as platelets recovered. This discussion highlights that a single initial SRA result may not represent the entire disease trajectory and underscores the importance of serial monitoring to guide safe transition from parenteral agents back to oral anticoagulation.
